label: Fluorine, in vivo agents
reference: CFCl3 (trichlorofluoromethane, Freon-11) at 0 ppm, the IUPAC primary reference for 19F. Nothing used in vivo resonates anywhere near 0, so scanners are calibrated against a secondary standard in the field of view: trifluoroacetic acid at -76.55 ppm or aqueous NaF at about -121.5 ppm. Beware that the 5-fluorouracil literature almost always renumbers its own axis with 5-FU itself at 0 ppm.
note: Downfield is positive and to the left, and the agents here alone spread over about 126 ppm, roughly 15 kHz at 3T, while organofluorine as a whole covers more than 300 ppm (over 800 ppm if inorganic fluorides are counted), so no single excitation pulse can cover this table and every 19F acquisition is centred on one resonance of one compound at a time.

peaks.name: Fluoxetine
peaks.full: Fluoxetine (aromatic CF3), detected together with norfluoxetine
peaks.note: Aryl-CF3 on the para-substituted phenoxy ring, three equivalent fluorines on one line. The in vivo brain signal is fluoxetine plus its active metabolite norfluoxetine, unresolved, at roughly 10 to 20 micromolar, which is only reachable with unlocalised or very coarsely localised acquisition over tens of minutes. Position taken from the aryl-CF3 family rather than from a directly quoted in vivo value, so treat it as approximate.

peaks.name: PFOB CF2Br
peaks.note: The most downfield of the perflubron lines, 2 of its 17 fluorines. PFOB is about 66 M in total fluorine but splits that over six resonances spanning more than 60 ppm, so imaging any single line discards most of the payload.

peaks.name: Sevo CF3
peaks.full: Sevoflurane, the two equivalent CF3 groups
peaks.note: Six chemically equivalent fluorines on one line, which makes sevoflurane the easiest volatile anaesthetic to detect. High-resolution value -75.13 ppm; the hexafluoroisopropyl CF3 pair is a doublet from coupling to the methine proton.

peaks.name: Iso CF3
peaks.note: The line responsible for isoflurane contamination and chemical shift displacement artefact in preclinical 19F MRI. In vivo and neat-liquid scanner measurements put it between -80.5 and -82.9 ppm, about 9 to 11 ppm downfield of PFCE; high-resolution solution work quotes it several ppm further downfield, and the discrepancy is a referencing and lipid-partitioning question that is not settled. It falls within about 1 ppm of the PFOB CF3 line.

peaks.name: PFOB CF3
peaks.note: The PFOB line usually imaged, 3 of 17 fluorines, so about 82 percent of the injected fluorine is thrown away. Its near-coincidence with the isoflurane CF3 resonance is exactly why isoflurane-anaesthetised PFOB studies need a suppression pulse or a narrow excitation.

peaks.name: Desflurane
peaks.full: Desflurane, CF3 and OCHF2 lines plotted as one stem
peaks.note: Desflurane (CF3-CHF-O-CHF2) gives three resonances: the CF3 and the OCHF2 fall close together in the -85 ppm region and are drawn here as a single stem, while the lone methine CHF sits far upfield beyond -140 ppm. Treat this position as approximate; no verified in vivo assignment was located and desflurane is rarely quantified by MRS.

peaks.name: Iso OCHF2
peaks.note: The second isoflurane resonance, consistently measured 6 to 7 ppm upfield of the CF3 line. It is J-coupled and appears as a multiplet rather than a singlet, and it lies only a few ppm from PFCE, which is why PFCE cell-tracking studies have to deal with it.

peaks.name: PFCE
peaks.note: Twenty chemically equivalent fluorines on a single line, about 61 M in 19F when neat, which is why PFCE dominates cell labelling and why it is the benchmark for 19F detection limits (about 12 mM 19F at 3T). Reported between -91.5 and -92.0 ppm.

peaks.name: PFOB CF2a
peaks.note: First of the internal CF2 components. The PFOB CF3 to CF2 spread of about 36 ppm is roughly 4.3 kHz at 3T, far more than any practical readout bandwidth can hold in one pixel.

peaks.name: Fluoride
peaks.note: Aqueous F-, the external reference phantom of choice when isoflurane rules out trifluoroacetic acid (KF sits about 4 ppm further upfield). Endogenous plasma fluoride is only about 1 micromolar and is undetectable, and the far larger skeletal pool is rigid-lattice fluorapatite with T2 of tens of microseconds, so it never appears in a liquid-state spectrum.

peaks.name: PFOB CF2b
peaks.note: The bulk of the internal CF2 fluorines, several groups overlapping into one envelope. This is the largest single feature of the PFOB spectrum and it is not the line anyone images.

peaks.name: PFOB CF2c
peaks.note: The most upfield perflubron line. From CF2Br to here is about 63 ppm, roughly 7.6 kHz at 3T and 17.7 kHz at 7T, which is the clearest single argument for choosing a one-line agent.

peaks.name: Sevo CH2F
peaks.note: The single fluoromethyl fluorine of the same molecule whose CF3 line sits at -75.1 ppm: one compound, two peaks about 80 ppm apart, which is roughly 9.7 kHz at 3T. No single excitation pulse covers both, and the CH2F line carries only one sixth of the CF3 signal.

peaks.name: FNuct
peaks.full: 5-FU fluoronucleotides (FdUMP, FUMP, FUTP and related anabolites)
peaks.note: The cytotoxic anabolites, 4.5 to 5 ppm downfield of 5-FU. The individual species are resolved in vitro but not in vivo, and the position is pH dependent. Fluoronucleosides resonate about 3.5 ppm downfield of 5-FU, between this peak and the parent drug.

peaks.name: HFB
peaks.note: Six equivalent fluorines on one line, about 52 M in 19F. Used as an injected pO2 reporter because R1 is linear in pO2 through collisional relaxation by dissolved oxygen; it reports only where the droplet sits, so it measures a point, not a tumour. Its near-coincidence with the 5-FU anabolite region is accidental but worth knowing.

peaks.name: 5-FU
peaks.note: The parent drug, a ring fluorine on the pyrimidine. In human liver it clears within 17 to 26 min after bolus, so it is often the smaller peak by the time a spectrum is averaged. The clinical literature usually sets this resonance to 0 ppm and quotes everything else relative to it, so a reported -19 ppm there means FBAL, not an absolute shift.

peaks.name: FUPA
peaks.note: The intermediate catabolite, about 17.3 ppm upfield of 5-FU and only about 1.3 ppm from FBAL, so the pair separates only with a good shim. Absolute position derived from the published offset from 5-FU rather than measured directly.

peaks.name: FBAL
peaks.note: The dominant catabolite and usually the tallest peak in a human liver 5-FU study, about 18.6 ppm upfield of 5-FU (a 2.2 kHz gap at 3T). It plateaus near 1.0 mM at about 60 min, roughly 20 percent of the injected dose, with T1 about 1.6 s at 1.5T. Sp3 CHF fluorines resonate well upfield of the ring fluorine of the parent, so the catabolites are always to the right of 5-FU and the anabolites to the left.
